text:
ashley: hey — I got a trace link from Datadog for a 502 we saw in prod, but the trace spans only show internal spans. How do I get the original request log lines (req_id header) from console or CLI?

ashley: the trace UI has this URL: https://dd.example.com/trace/abc123 — there's a span tag `http.request_id: rq_7f8a` but i can't find the raw logs for that req id. :thinking_face:

ashley: any quick pointers? i tried searching logs for rq_7f8a and only found app logs, not the loadbalancer request line we need.

@dave: paste the span attributes? usually there are two helpful bits: the request_id and the span's service/host.

ashley: pasted: service: gateway, host: gw-12, http.request_id: rq_7f8a, dd.env: prod

maria: simplest flow i use: 1) from the trace span, copy the request_id value (rq_7f8a). 2) use the logs console with a combined query: `service:gateway host:gw-12 @http.request_id:rq_7f8a` — that usually surfaces both LB and app logs. if that doesn't work, expand to `@request_id:rq_7f8a OR @http.request_id:rq_7f8a` (different components name the field differently).

maria: if you're on the CLI, here's the jq/grep trick we use to map trace -> raw request lines (assuming logs are exported to our s3/raw-logs prefix):

```
# list recent raw log objects that contain the request id
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-raw-logs/prod/ | awk '{print $4}' | xargs -n1 -I{} bash -c "aws s3 cp s3://redwood-raw-logs/prod/{} - | grep -i 'rq_7f8a' -n && echo found in {}"
```

maria: for Console quick-hunt: Open Logs > Add filter: env:prod, service:gateway, then in message text search `rq_7f8a`. Sometimes the LB logs are ingested under a different service like `nginx-lb` so try a broader service filter if nothing shows.

ashley: thanks — i see a `request_id` formatted as `req=rq_7f8a` in the LB lines. so i should search message contains `req=rq_7f8a`?

maria: yes, exact match helps: `message:"req=rq_7f8a"` or use wildcard `req=rq_7f8*` if there are truncations. Also check for headers: `@headers.request_id:"rq_7f8a"`.

@dave: if you only have trace id and not request_id, you can map by span.trace_id -> logs by looking for the trace id in logs (`trace_id:abc123`). But note not all logs include trace_id. We enrich spans with request ids; that's the most reliable link.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: prod/gateway rolled v2.14.3 @ 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z — no errors in deploy logs.

ashley: quick follow-up — any recommended saved dashboard for this? want to add a one-click link for trace->logs hunting.

maria: we have a saved logs view: https://dd.example.com/logs?view=redwood/trace-hunt — it pre-fills common filters (env, service, message). i'll add a short runbook entry to the infra wiki with the cli snippet.

ashley: perfect, thanks both. saved me a bunch of time. :thumbsup:
